winRate.short: The share of your closed trades that ended in profit.
winRate.example: Example: 6 winners out of 10 closed trades = 60%.
winRate.caveat: Break-even trades count in the denominator, not as wins; win rate alone does not show profitability.

profitFactor.short: Gross profit divided by gross loss across your closed trades.
profitFactor.example: Example: you won $3,000 and lost $2,000 ⇒ 1.5; above 1 means a net profit.
profitFactor.caveat: With no losses at all it reads ∞; computed before commissions.

avgR.short: Average R of closed trades with a stop; R = profit ÷ initial risk, by direction (LONG/SHORT).
avgR.caveat: A trade without a stop is excluded, not counted as 0R.

expectancy.short: The average R you made per closed trade, with break-even trades in the denominator.
expectancy.example: Example: half the trades win +2R and half lose −1R ⇒ +0.5R per trade.

sharpe.short: Mean R per trade divided by the standard deviation of R.
sharpe.example: Example: an average of +0.5R with a 1R standard deviation ⇒ 0.5.
sharpe.caveat: No risk-free rate and no annualizing — not comparable to a fund's Sharpe ratio.

maxDD.short: The largest drop, in money, from a peak in your cumulative closed-trade P&L to the low after it.
maxDD.example: Example: cumulative P&L rose to $2,000 and fell to $1,200 ⇒ $800.
maxDD.caveat: Measured as an amount, not as a percentage of capital.

avgWin.short: The average profit on your closed trades that ended in profit.

avgLoss.short: The average loss on your closed trades that ended in a loss.

avgHold.short: The average number of days between entry and exit on closed trades.
avgHold.example: Example: trades of 2 and 6 days ⇒ 4 days.
avgHold.caveat: Rounded calendar days; same-day entry and exit = 0.

equityCurve.short: Your account balance over time: your capital base plus cumulative P&L after each closed trade.
equityCurve.caveat: Each point is a closing day; open positions excluded.

totalReturn.short: Your closed-trade P&L as a percentage of the capital base you set.

winStreak.short: The number of profitable trades in a row, up to your latest closed trade.
winStreak.example: Example: 3 wins in a row ⇒ 3; the line below shows your best streak.
winStreak.caveat: A losing streak shows as 0, not as a negative number.

grade.short: An A–F grade for the month: 40% win rate, 30% R, 20% discipline, 10% consistency.
grade.caveat: Discipline is the self-reported 'followed my plan' flag.

entryQuality.short: A 1–5 star rating you gave your entry: how well timing, price and confirmation matched the plan.
entryQuality.example: Example: you entered at your planned price after confirmation ⇒ 5 stars.

accountEquity.short: The capital base you set plus cumulative P&L from closed and open trades.
accountEquity.caveat: Per-trade risk is sized from your fixed capital base, not current equity.

streakHistory.short: Your winning and losing streaks in time order, one bar per streak.
streakHistory.example: Example: 3 wins then 2 losses ⇒ two bars, 3 and 2.

dayOfWeek.short: Cumulative P&L by the weekday you entered the trade.
dayOfWeek.example: Example: a trade opened Monday and closed Wednesday counts for Monday.

performanceBySetup.short: One card per setup you traded: trade count, win rate and total R.

winRateBySetup.short: Bar height is the setup's win rate; the number above it is the trade count.
winRateBySetup.example: Example: a purple bar = 50% or more, a gray bar = below 50%.

bestDay.short: The weekday with the highest total P&L, by entry day.
bestDay.caveat: Trade count is not taken into account.

bestSetup.short: The setup with the highest win rate; on a tie, the one with more trades.
bestSetup.example: Example: Pullback at 70% over 10 trades ranks above Breakout at 60%.
bestSetup.caveat: No minimum sample: one trade at 100% can win. Unknown is excluded.

bestEmotion.short: The entry emotion you marked with the highest win rate; on a tie, the one with more trades.
bestEmotion.example: Example: Calm at 65% ranks above Confident at 55%.

rDistribution.short: How many closed trades fell in each R range, losses left to wins right.
rDistribution.example: Example: a +1.4R trade counts in the 1R to 2R range.
rDistribution.caveat: Trades without a stop are not counted.

pnlByMonth.short: The sum of closed-trade P&L for each month, by trade date.
pnlByMonth.caveat: A trade not converted to your capital currency is not counted.

emotionPerformance.short: Total closed-trade P&L by the emotion you marked at entry.
emotionPerformance.caveat: A trade with no emotion marked counts as Unknown.

setupMatrix.short: A table per setup: trades, win rate, average R and P&L, sorted by P&L.

holdTimeVsPnl.short: Each dot is a closed trade: holding days against P&L.
holdTimeVsPnl.example: Example: a dot at 5 days and +$300 = held 5 days, made $300.
holdTimeVsPnl.caveat: Trades not converted to your capital currency are not shown.

rr.short: The ratio between your risk and the potential reward, written risk:reward.
rr.example: Example: a stop $2 below entry and a target $6 above ⇒ 1:3.

rMultiple.short: A trade's result in units of initial risk: LONG (Exit − Entry), SHORT (Entry − Exit).
rMultiple.example: Example: you risked $50 and lost $100 ⇒ −2R; the stop was not honored.

mfeMae.short: How far a trade ran in your favor (MFE) and against you (MAE) before it closed.
mfeMae.example: Example: entry $100, high $106, low $97 ⇒ MFE $6, MAE $3.
mfeMae.caveat: Only if you filled in the fields.

wilson.short: The lower bound of your 'true' win rate at 95% confidence — cautious when trades are few.
wilson.example: Example: 3 wins out of 3 = 100%, but the lower bound is about 44%.

rrBucket3plus.short: Trades whose planned ratio, stop versus target, is 1:3 or more.
rrBucket3plus.example: Example: a stop $1 below entry and a target $3.50 above ⇒ 1:3.5 ⇒ in the group.
rrBucket3plus.caveat: At 1:3, a 25% win rate breaks even, before commissions.

dna.short: Four 0–100 scores — risk, discipline, consistency, growth — from your closed trades.
dna.example: Example: 2% average risk per trade ⇒ risk score 50.
dna.caveat: Discipline is the self-reported 'followed my plan' flag.

edge.short: Setup-and-emotion pairs where your win rate and R are strongest, ranked by Wilson score.
edge.example: Example: Breakout + Calm · 4 of 5 won · average +1.2R.
edge.caveat: Needs 3+ trades; a ranking, not a significance test.

antiEdge.short: Setup-and-emotion pairs where your win rate is below 50% or your average R is negative.
antiEdge.example: Example: Breakout + FOMO · 1 win out of 4 · average R −0.8R.
antiEdge.caveat: Needs at least 2 trades; up to 5 are shown.

tilt.short: An emotional state that pushes you off your rules, usually after losses.
tilt.example: Example: 3 losses in a row ⇒ Tilt Shield warns before the next trade.
tilt.caveat: Rule of thumb: take a break after 2 consecutive losses.

marketRegime.short: The market environment, read from SPY/QQQ versus their 20-day average, sector breadth and volatility.
marketRegime.example: Example: price above a rising 20-day average with most sectors rising ⇒ Bull Trend.
marketRegime.caveat: Based on market prices, not your trades.

discipline.short: The share of your closed trades you marked 'followed my plan'.
discipline.caveat: Self-reported; an unmarked trade is not counted.

dnaRisk.short: A 0–100 score from your average risk per trade as a percentage of capital.
dnaRisk.caveat: Does not measure whether you honored the stop.

dnaConsistency.short: A 0–100 score from the spread of your R outcomes; less spread scores higher.

dnaGrowth.short: A 0–100 score from the slope of cumulative R over your last 20 closed trades; 50 = flat.
dnaGrowth.example: Example: cumulative R rising about +0.5R per trade ⇒ about 75.

setup.short: Your entry pattern — the exact conditions under which you take a position.
setup.example: Example: Breakout, Pullback or Bull Flag.

riskPerTrade.short: The percentage of capital you accept to lose on one trade if the stop is hit.
riskPerTrade.example: Example: $10,000 capital and 1% risk ⇒ a $100 maximum loss.

riskLimits.short: Your per-trade risk, plus a cap on all open positions: 2× it, between 3% and 5%.
riskLimits.caveat: Cap ÷ per-trade risk = how many full-size positions fit at once.

positionSize.short: Shares = (capital × risk %) ÷ the distance between entry and stop.

stopLoss.short: The price you set in advance to exit a losing trade, capping the loss at your plan.
stopLoss.example: Example: LONG at $50, stop below support at $48 ⇒ $2 risk per share.
stopLoss.caveat: R and position size use the saved stop.

takeProfit.short: The target price you set to close a winning trade.
takeProfit.example: Example: entry $100 and stop $98 ⇒ a default target of $104 (1:2).
takeProfit.caveat: The default on the chart and in the coach is 1:2.

breakout.short: Entering when price breaks above a key resistance level, ideally on rising volume.
breakout.example: Example: resistance at $50 and a daily close at $51 on twice the average volume.

pullback.short: Entering when an uptrending price pulls back to support and then resumes higher.
pullback.example: Example: a run from $40 to $50, a pullback to the moving average at $46, entry there.

bullFlag.short: A tight, slightly falling consolidation after a sharp rise, on shrinking volume.
bullFlag.example: Example: a rise from $20 to $26, then 5 days in a $25–$26 range.

ORBBreakout.short: A break of the high or low of the first 5, 15 or 30 minutes of trading.
ORBBreakout.example: Example: a first-15-minute range of $30–$31 ⇒ entry above $31.

VWAPReclaim.short: Price reclaims VWAP — the day's volume-weighted average price — after dipping below it.
VWAPReclaim.example: Example: VWAP at $40, a dip to $39.50, then back above $40 on volume.

higherLow.short: Each pullback stops above the previous low — the mark of an uptrend.

cupAndHandle.short: A U-shaped base followed by a short, shallow dip (the handle) before a breakout.
cupAndHandle.example: Example: a fall from $60 to $48, back to $59, a handle down to $56, a break above $59.

failedBreakout.short: A breakout that quickly falls back below the broken level — a trap for late buyers.
failedBreakout.example: Example: a break to $51 above $50, back to $49 within a day ⇒ SHORT.

overextendedFade.short: A counter-trend trade when price is unusually far above the 20 EMA.
overextendedFade.example: Example: a stock at $60 with the 20 EMA at $52 ⇒ SHORT toward the average.
overextendedFade.caveat: The app sets no threshold for 'far' — it is yours.

EMABounce50.short: A pullback to the 50-day exponential moving average on a daily chart, and a bounce off it.
EMABounce50.example: Example: 50 EMA at $80, a daily low of $80.20 and a close at $82.

trendContinuation.short: Entering on a shallow pullback to the 9 EMA within an established trend.
trendContinuation.example: Example: a pullback to the 9 EMA at $30.10, entry at $30.30, stop at $29.80.

gapAndGo.short: A stock that gaps up at the open and keeps rising without filling the gap.
gapAndGo.example: Example: a $20 close, a $22 open and a $24 high without trading below $22.

earningsGapPlay.short: Trading in the direction of the gap that opens after an earnings report — up or down.
earningsGapPlay.example: Example: a +6% gap ⇒ LONG above the opening high; a −6% gap ⇒ SHORT below the opening low.

rangeBreakout.short: A break out of a price range that lasted days or weeks.
rangeBreakout.example: Example: 3 weeks between $40 and $44, then a close at $45.

postEarningsStrength.short: A stock that holds above an upside gap in the days after a strong report.
postEarningsStrength.example: Example: a gap from $50 to $56, then 5 days above $55.

powerHourBreak.short: A breakout in the last trading hour, 3–4 pm New York time.
powerHourBreak.example: Example: a $70 daily high broken at 3:20 pm ⇒ entry at $70.10.

MOCFade.short: Trading against a sharp move into the close (Market-On-Close), expecting a next-day pullback.
MOCFade.example: Example: a +4% move in the last hour ⇒ SHORT into the close.
MOCFade.caveat: On the NYSE, MOC orders are accepted until 3:50 p.m. New York time.

overnightHold.short: A trade you left open past the trading-day close.
overnightHold.example: Example: you bought at $30 at 3:30 p.m. and the stock opened at $28 the next day ⇒ a gap against you.
overnightHold.caveat: A stop does not protect against an opening gap.

overnightReversal.short: Trading against the overnight move at the open, after confirmation.
overnightReversal.example: Example: a −3% gap at the open and price back above the opening price ⇒ LONG.

supportBounce.short: Entering when price drops to a known support level and turns up.
supportBounce.example: Example: support at $25, a low of $25.10, entry at $25.60, stop at $24.80.

resistanceBreak.short: Entering when price breaks a specific resistance level that stopped it before.
resistanceBreak.example: Example: stopped twice at $80, then a close at $81 on high volume.

pullback20EMA.short: Entering when an uptrending price pulls back to the 20-period exponential moving average and turns.
pullback20EMA.example: Example: 20 EMA at $40, a low of $40.15 and a close at $41.

emotionConfident.short: Confidence grounded in a valid setup and analysis, not in a winning streak.
emotionConfident.example: Example: every condition you wrote down was met and you entered at normal size.
emotionConfident.caveat: After a winning streak, check that it is not overconfidence.

emotionCalm.short: You entered without pressure or chasing, according to plan.
emotionCalm.example: Example: you waited for your planned price and set the stop and target in advance.

emotionPatient.short: You waited for a setup that met all your criteria instead of entering every move.
emotionPatient.example: Example: you skipped two weak breakouts and took the third.

emotionNeutral.short: You entered with no emotional charge — neither excited nor fearful.
emotionNeutral.example: Example: one more trade from the plan, with no special expectation.

emotionHesitant.short: You hesitated at entry — usually when the setup is unclear or confidence is low.
emotionHesitant.example: Example: you waited for one more candle and entered $0.50 above your planned price.

emotionNervous.short: Tension that clouded your judgment during the trade.
emotionNervous.example: Example: you checked the price every minute and moved the stop twice.
emotionNervous.caveat: Sometimes a sign the position is too large.

emotionFOMO.short: You entered because price moved hard and you feared missing out, with no valid setup.
emotionFOMO.example: Example: the stock was up +6% and you entered at the high with no clear stop.

emotionAngry.short: Anger after a loss that pushed you to win it back at once — revenge trading.
emotionAngry.example: Example: you lost $200 and immediately opened a trade at double size.

chartCalcPosition.short: Fills the position calculator from the chart: ticker, live price as entry, a stop and a 1:2 target.

chartAddToJournal.short: Opens a journal trade from the chart, prefilled with ticker, live price, a stop and a 1:2 target.
chartAddToJournal.example: Example: entry $50, stop $48 and target $54 filled in, and you save.

visionOcr.short: Reads a trade from a chart screenshot and fills the fields instead of typing.
visionOcr.example: Example: you uploaded a screenshot with entry, stop and target ⇒ the fields were filled.
